key_insight: A hybrid nanocone-nanohole texture boosts thin-film silicon solar-cell light trapping by reducing front reflection and strengthening internal optical confinement.
engineering_relevance: The design offers a practical route to higher-efficiency, thermally robust thin-film silicon photovoltaics without increasing absorber thickness.
method: Front-surface silicon nanocones create a graded refractive-index transition to suppress reflection.
Embedded air-filled nanoholes increase scattering and internal reflection for longer-wavelength absorption.
FDTD optics optimization is coupled with electrical and opto-thermal device modeling to tune structure and operating conditions.
evidence_signal: Optimized simulations report 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% fill factor, and 24.42% efficiency, with 95.21% efficiency retained up to 45°C.
watch_item: The reported gains are simulation-based, so fabrication tolerance, nanostructure uniformity, and large-area manufacturability remain key validation concerns.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
